subject: Medicore: Dedicated inference ops, isolation needs & SLA summary
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Claire Donovan <claire@medicore.com>, Benji Ortiz <benji.ortiz@medicore.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Medicore: Dedicated inference ops, isolation needs & SLA summary

Hi Claire / Benji —

Thanks for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared baseline and clear next steps. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Top pain points you highlighted
- P95 latency spikes when concurrency > 200 requests/min (affects user-facing triage flow)
- Need for tenant isolation: PHI workloads require a dedicated environment and stricter audit/retention controls
- Cost predictability: procurement wants a committed monthly spend with clear overage rules

Goals we agreed on
- Launch a canary pilot running the triage model in a dedicated pool (isolated tenancy) for 4–6 weeks
- Target production SLOs: p95 <= 250ms for text-generation endpoints, and 99.9% uptime for the dedicated pool
- Provide SOC2 evidence, KMS integration guidance, and audit-log access for your compliance team

Redwood recommendation (high level)
1) Dedicated reserved GPU pool (isolated, customer-only tenant) sized for baseline concurrency with burst slots for traffic peaks.
2) Canary plan: 4-week pilot with a 2-week internal validation window, then a customer-facing ramp.
3) Ops: we’ll provision prefix/KV caching for hot prompts, suggest mixed quantization (int8) for the streamer model to reduce token cost, and enable continuous batching tuned to your latency targets.
4) SLA: propose 99.9% availability for the pool with latency SLOs tied to model route. Credits for SLA breaches outlined in attached draft.

Open questions / decisions needed from Medicore
- Procurement: preferred cadence for a monthly reserved commitment (3 / 6 / 12 months)?
- Security: confirm KMS vendor (AWS KMS / Okta / other) and whether you require HSM-backed keys
- Pilot: agree on a start date and a success criterion (e.g., p95 latency, error rate, and cost per 1k inference tokens)

Attachments: medicore_mop_v1.pdf (MOP + checklist), SLA-draft-medicore-20270620.docx (working draft)

Next steps I’ll take
- Naomi will draft the canary runbook and initial capacity estimate tomorrow
- Aditya will surface quantization and cost-estimate options by Monday
- I’ll send an updated SLA draft with explicit latency targets and credit bands by EOD Monday

Would love a short reply that confirms the procurement window you prefer and whether SOC2 docs should be sent to procurement@medicore.com or security@medicore.com.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — super clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Procurement cadence: leaning toward a 6-month reserved commitment to start (easier for budget this quarter). We may convert to 12 months after pilot.
2) Burst behavior: during peak periods (clinical shift changes) we see 3–4x baseline spikes for ~10–15 minutes. Can Redwood guarantee burst capacity or should we architect a fallback?
3) SOC2: please send evidence to security@medicore.com. Procurement will want a copy of the SLA draft and a short TCO estimate.

Also attaching our internal procurement checklist (procurement_checklist_medicore.pdf) — happy for Naomi to review and call out any gaps.

Claire

Claire — thanks. Quick answers inline and a slightly expanded ops plan: 

On burst: Redwood supports two patterns for short bursts:
- Reserved + burst pool: reserved capacity handles baseline; bursts billed at a predictable overage rate with pre-warmed burst nodes available (we can guarantee slot availability for X% of expected peaks with a burst SLA).
- Fallback routing: route non-critical requests to a compatible lower-cost model variant when capacity is saturated (no impact to PHI flows if you prefer full isolation).

Recommendation: for Medicore’s use-case we recommend reserved baseline sized for 1.2x measured baseline and a small pre-warmed burst allocation sized to cover ~75% of observed 10–15 minute spikes. That balances cost and availability. Naomi’s attached runbook has a suggested sizing table.

SLA / credits: attached sla-draft-medicore-20270620.docx includes availability credit tiers and a latency remediation clause tied to route-level p95s. We can bake the credit percentages into the commercial SOW.

Compliance: we’ll send SOC2 artifacts to security@medicore.com today and confirm KMS options. For audit logs we expose per-request tracing and retention controls in the console; we’ll map the retention window to your data-retention policy in the pilot.

Proposed pilot timeline
- Week 0: legal + procurement sign-off (SLA and SOW)
- Week 1–2: provisioning, model rollout into dedicated pool, internal validation (smoke + perf)
- Week 3–6: canary with limited user group, collect cost/latency metrics, iterate

I’ve asked Naomi to schedule a 30-minute ops alignment call next week to agree on the runbook and the precise GPU SKU mix.

Best,
Marcus

Appreciate the detail — this looks like the right approach. A few items from procurement/security that will block a kickoff until cleared:

- SOC2 evidence: please send the report and the customer-facing summary to security@medicore.com (Claire requested this).
- Audit logs: we need confirmation that logs can be exported daily to our S3 bucket and retained for a minimum of 2 years.
- KMS: we use AWS KMS with a customer-managed key; please include HSM option pricing if available.

Pilot acceptance: we’ll aim to sign procurement paperwork for a 6-month reserved commitment conditioned on a successful canary (success defined as p95 <= 250ms and error rate < 1%). If we can get the SOC2 artifacts and the S3-log export confirmation this week, procurement can move quickly.

Benji Ortiz
